## Python — `src/gamestudio/`

- `src/gamestudio/__init__.py` — Game asset generation studio.
- `src/gamestudio/api/app.py` — The studio's HTTP API: the surface the desktop application consumes.
- `src/gamestudio/api/auth.py` — The token that protects the local API, and the host it answers.
- `src/gamestudio/blender/bl_common.py` — Utilities shared by the scripts that run INSIDE Blender.
- `src/gamestudio/blender/bl_make_fixture.py` — Generate a rigged and animated test entity, exported as glTF.
- `src/gamestudio/blender/bl_render_ortho.py` — Multi-direction orthographic render of an animated 3D character.
- `src/gamestudio/blender/run.py` — Running Blender headless.
- `src/gamestudio/cli.py` — The studio's command-line interface.
- `src/gamestudio/config.py` — Global configuration, read from the environment (optional .env).
- `src/gamestudio/domain/gltf.py` — Lightweight reading of a glTF/GLB file, with no dependency and no Blender.
- `src/gamestudio/domain/models.py` — The studio's data model.
- `src/gamestudio/domain/recipe.py` — Loading and writing recipes (project YAML documents).
- `src/gamestudio/domain/skeleton.py` — Skeleton convention: the bone names the studio, Blender and Godot share.
- `src/gamestudio/godot/spriteframes.py` — Generation of a Godot SpriteFrames resource from sprite sheets.
- `src/gamestudio/godot/tscn.py` — Writing Godot 4 scene files (.tscn) and resources (.tres).
- `src/gamestudio/godot/tscn_edit.py` — Editing an existing Godot 4 scene: reading and rewriting a node's properties.
- `src/gamestudio/godot/vfx_scene.py` — Godot scenes of an effect: a flipbook, and optionally an emitter that uses it.
- `src/gamestudio/jobs/queue.py` — Job queue backed by SQLite.
- `src/gamestudio/jobs/supervisor.py` — Running the worker in the background of the web server.
- `src/gamestudio/jobs/worker.py` — Worker: consumes the queue and runs the long jobs.
- `src/gamestudio/mcp_server.py` — MCP server: the studio, driven by an agent.
- `src/gamestudio/net.py` — Check the listening port before starting the server.
- `src/gamestudio/pipeline/base.py` — Foundation of the pipeline graph: shared context, steps, fingerprints.
- `src/gamestudio/pipeline/graph.py` — Orchestration: from an entity's description to its Godot files.
- `src/gamestudio/pipeline/steps/export.py` — Export steps: writing into the Godot project.
- `src/gamestudio/pipeline/steps/generation.py` — Steps that call a paid service (Runware, Tripo): style, LoRA, posed reference, matting, 3D.
- `src/gamestudio/pipeline/steps/render.py` — Rendering a 3D mesh into sprite sheets, one per animation and per direction.
- `src/gamestudio/runware/catalog.py` — AIR identifiers of the models the studio uses.
- `src/gamestudio/runware/client.py` — HTTP client of the Runware API.
- `src/gamestudio/runware/errors.py` — Runware API errors, kept apart from the studio's own.
- `src/gamestudio/service/__init__.py` — Business layer of the studio: what its three interfaces can do.
- `src/gamestudio/service/activity.py` — What the studio is doing right now: renders under way or queued, agents writing data.
- `src/gamestudio/service/briefing.py` — The briefing: what an agent must know about the studio before working in it.
- `src/gamestudio/service/cards.py` — A game design card's workbench: its render, its sketch, its generated images.
- `src/gamestudio/service/catalog.py` — Reading the studio's state: environment, projects, characters, assets.
- `src/gamestudio/service/codemap.py` — The code map: what lives where in the repository, one line per file.
- `src/gamestudio/service/colors.py` — A game's colors: each one written in its files, by aspect of the art direction, and where.
- `src/gamestudio/service/connections.py` — MCP connections: what is plugged in, where it is declared, and whether it can start.
- `src/gamestudio/service/context.py` — Root of the studio's data, shared by every interface.
- `src/gamestudio/service/direction_chat.py` — A conversation on the graphic style or the game type, with an agent the studio drives.
- `src/gamestudio/service/doctor.py` — The diagnosis: what works here, what is missing, and what to do.
- `src/gamestudio/service/documents.py` — A project's documents: texts that are written, reread and kept.
- `src/gamestudio/service/effects.py` — A project's visual effects: specs that are written, sheets that are rendered.
- `src/gamestudio/service/entities.py` — A world card's workbench: from the card to concepts, then to 3D.
- `src/gamestudio/service/errors.py` — Business errors of the service layer, translated by each interface.
- `src/gamestudio/service/folders.py` — Open a folder of the machine as a studio project.
- `src/gamestudio/service/fonts.py` — A game's typography: its font files, its font resources, the sizes and the texts its scenes use.
- `src/gamestudio/service/forge.py` — The icon forge: create an icon, a whole set, or redo one -- all the way into the game.
- `src/gamestudio/service/handoff.py` — Handoff: entrust a piece of work to an agent, which carries it through to the end.
- `src/gamestudio/service/images.py` — Preview rendering: an asset image scaled down to a reasonable size.
- `src/gamestudio/service/inbox.py` — The inbox: what one drops into the studio to hand to an agent.
- `src/gamestudio/service/influences.py` — The art direction's leading aspects: graphic style and game type, their cards and influences.
- `src/gamestudio/service/jobs.py` — Job queue: state, detail, and a stream of changes.
- `src/gamestudio/service/library.py` — Readable library: browsing, syncing, filing.
- `src/gamestudio/service/lookdev.py` — A game's lookdev: each element of its art direction, taken out of the game, shown alone and live.
- `src/gamestudio/service/meshes.py` — 3D meshes: where they come from, and how they enter the studio.
- `src/gamestudio/service/poses.py` — Poses: the one imposed on a concept, and the one read from an image.
- `src/gamestudio/service/preview_data.py` — A game's preview data: fake server answers, so a screen that needs a server renders full.
- `src/gamestudio/service/produce.py` — Production operations: everything that costs money, everything that takes time.
- `src/gamestudio/service/prompts.py` — Workbench prompts: what the model is asked for to get a reference.
- `src/gamestudio/service/renders.py` — A game's renders: one of its scenes, drawn by its own engine, off screen.
- `src/gamestudio/service/screen_comments.py` — Comments on a screen's elements: what the user asks of each one, sent to an agent in turn.
- `src/gamestudio/service/screens.py` — The screen editor: a game screen, its Controls, their properties, written on its branch.
- `src/gamestudio/service/sheets.py` — Import of outside files: a single image, or a sheet to split.
- `src/gamestudio/service/showcase.py` — The icons and props showcase: each element of the game shown as it is, to be judged.
- `src/gamestudio/service/skills.py` — The studio's skills: what they are, whether they hold up, and their index.
- `src/gamestudio/service/survey.py` — A game's survey: what its folder already contains, read without running anything.
- `src/gamestudio/service/trash.py` — A project's trash: what the studio removes from the game, kept so it can be put back.
- `src/gamestudio/service/video.py` — Reference video: extract a batch of usable frames from it.
- `src/gamestudio/service/workspace.py` — The workspace: every project summarised, with a readable report for each.
- `src/gamestudio/service/world.py` — A project's world: sections the user declares themselves.
- `src/gamestudio/sheet/__init__.py` — Sheets: a file that holds several elements, split into single files.
- `src/gamestudio/sheet/bitmap.py` — Splitting a PNG sheet into one file per element.
- `src/gamestudio/sheet/importer.py` — Bringing a sheet into the studio: store, database, library.
- `src/gamestudio/sheet/layout.py` — What does not depend on the medium: boxes, grouping, order, names.
- `src/gamestudio/sprites.py` — Assembling sprite sheets from Blender renders.
- `src/gamestudio/store/assets.py` — Storage of produced files, addressed by the hash of their content.
- `src/gamestudio/store/curation.py` — What the user can do with the filing: file, rename, delete.
- `src/gamestudio/store/db.py` — SQLite persistence: jobs, assets, characters, style packs.
- `src/gamestudio/store/folders.py` — Project folders: a project is a folder on the machine.
- `src/gamestudio/store/library.py` — Readable mirror of the store: `<folder>/.gamestudio/library/`.
- `src/gamestudio/svg/__init__.py` — Splitting an SVG sheet: exact geometry, no external dependency.
- `src/gamestudio/svg/geometry.py` — Minimal SVG geometry: matrices, lengths, bounding boxes.
- `src/gamestudio/svg/raster.py` — Optional rasterization of an SVG icon to PNG.
- `src/gamestudio/svg/split.py` — Splitting an SVG sheet into one file per icon.
- `src/gamestudio/terminal/__init__.py` — The studio's terminal: agent tabs in their own window.
- `src/gamestudio/terminal/harnesses.py` — The catalog of agents a tab can launch.
- `src/gamestudio/terminal/routes.py` — The terminal's HTTP and WebSocket surface, mounted by `api/app.py`.
- `src/gamestudio/terminal/screen.py` — A tab's screen, saved to disk.
- `src/gamestudio/terminal/session.py` — A terminal tab: a PTY, what it has shown, and who is listening.
- `src/gamestudio/terminal/transcripts.py` — Reading, in an agent's native transcript, the moment it hands control back.
- `src/gamestudio/tripo/__init__.py` — The Tripo API, called directly: the studio's second 3D route.
- `src/gamestudio/tripo/catalog.py` — Tripo models, and what a call really costs.
- `src/gamestudio/tripo/client.py` — HTTP client of the Tripo API (v3), the direct route.
- `src/gamestudio/tripo/errors.py` — Tripo API errors, kept apart from the studio's own.
- `src/gamestudio/vfx/__init__.py` — Visual effects: a spec written in a computation language, rendered as a sheet.
- `src/gamestudio/vfx/expr.py` — The effects language: numpy expressions, evaluated over the whole image.
- `src/gamestudio/vfx/noise.py` — Procedural noises: the raw material of every effect.
- `src/gamestudio/vfx/render.py` — Rendering an effect: composited layers, post-processing, a sheet.
- `src/gamestudio/vfx/sim.py` — The two simulations of an effect: a fluid on a grid, free particles.
- `src/gamestudio/vfx/spec.py` — An effect's spec: a YAML document that says everything to render.
- `src/gamestudio/video/__init__.py` — Reference video: what it takes to draw usable frames from it.
- `src/gamestudio/video/contact.py` — Contact sheet: all frames of a batch in a single image.
- `src/gamestudio/video/frames.py` — Frame extraction: the plan first, ffmpeg next.
- `src/gamestudio/video/importer.py` — Bringing a video into the studio: store, database, manifest, contact sheet.
- `src/gamestudio/video/probe.py` — Probing a video: what ffprobe says about the file, and what is refused.
- `src/gamestudio/vision/__init__.py` — Local vision: the poses imposed on generation, and what is read from an image.
- `src/gamestudio/vision/detect.py` — What is read from an image, locally: its pose, and its cut-out silhouette.
- `src/gamestudio/vision/poses.py` — OpenPose reference poses: the ones imposed when generating a concept.

## React front — `app/src/`

- `app/src/App.tsx` — Application frame: navigation rail, active project, status bar.
- `app/src/api.ts` — Client of the studio API.
- `app/src/chat/ChatApp.tsx` — The Chats window: a strip of tabs, one terminal per tab.
- `app/src/chat/TerminalPane.tsx` — A tab: an xterm plugged into the server's stream.
- `app/src/chat/logos.tsx` — The agent providers' logos, by harness id.
- `app/src/chat/meta.ts` — What the Chats window remembers about a tab and the server does not know.
- `app/src/chat.tsx` — Entry point of the Chats window.
- `app/src/components/ActivityBar.tsx` — The global progress bar: what the studio is doing, along the status bar.
- `app/src/components/CardGenerate.tsx` — Generating for a card: text to image, or image to image from its sketch or its render.
- `app/src/components/CardReferences.tsx` — A card's references: the images the user adds to show what they want.
- `app/src/components/CardSketch.tsx` — A card's sketch: an Excalidraw, saved with it, exported as PNG for agents.
- `app/src/components/CardWorkspace.tsx` — The workbench of a game design card: its gestures, its visuals, its text.
- `app/src/components/ComparePicker.tsx` — Picking an image for a comparator slot.
- `app/src/components/CompareStage.tsx` — Visual comparator: the four ways to judge two images.
- `app/src/components/DirectionRoom.tsx` — The graphic style or the game type, in the Universe: its parts, its board of influences, and a thread with an agent.
- `app/src/components/Handoff.tsx` — Handing a brief to an agent: a new discussion, or a tab already open.
- `app/src/components/IconForge.tsx` — The icon forge in the showcase: create, redo, split, adopt, and remove.
- `app/src/components/JobLog.tsx` — A project's job log, and the report of each job.
- `app/src/components/LanguageChoice.tsx` — The language choice, at first launch: until it is made, the studio does not open.
- `app/src/components/Markdown.tsx` — A minimal Markdown renderer, for the texts the studio produces and reads.
- `app/src/components/MeshPreview.tsx` — A mesh in a frame: the studio scene reduced to what it takes to judge.
- `app/src/components/ModelPicker.tsx` — Choosing an image model: a dropdown, each model with its family, its traits and its price.
- `app/src/components/Scene3D.tsx` — The studio's 3D scene: a GLB, its shadings, its animations, Blender-style navigation.
- `app/src/components/ScreenEditor.tsx` — The editor of a game screen: point at an element on the render, say what it should become.
- `app/src/components/SpriteRender.tsx` — Rendering a 3D mesh into sprite sheets: the "Sprites" panel of the 3D space.
- `app/src/components/Station.tsx` — The station: what works on this machine, what is connected, what is followed.
- `app/src/components/Toasts.tsx` — The studio's messages: one card per event, bottom right, above the status bar.
- `app/src/components/UpdateProgress.tsx` — The studio rebuild, followed: its phases, a gauge, the current line.
- `app/src/components/ui.tsx` — The studio's interface vocabulary.
- `app/src/lib/catalog.ts` — The models the interface offers, and their unit price.
- `app/src/lib/host.ts` — What the shell can do and a web page cannot.
- `app/src/lib/i18n.ts` — The interface language: English as written in the code, or its French translation.
- `app/src/lib/paths.ts` — Disk paths as the interface shows them: a folder's name, a file revealed on disk.
- `app/src/lib/queries.ts` — Server reads, in one place.
- `app/src/lib/scene.ts` — What pages know about a 3D scene without loading three.js.
- `app/src/lib/scroll.ts` — Whole-pixel scrolling: a scroller left between two pixels is put back on one when it rests.
- `app/src/lib/store.tsx` — Application-wide state: active project, messages, job queue.
- `app/src/locales/fr.ts` — French translation of the interface: English text -> French text.
- `app/src/main.tsx` — Front-end entry point.
- `app/src/pages/Agents.tsx` — At work: the agents at work, and what they display, live.
- `app/src/pages/Compare.tsx` — Compare: two images or two meshes, under the same eye.
- `app/src/pages/Context.tsx` — Context: what every agent reads before working in the studio.
- `app/src/pages/Control.tsx` — Control room: decide, pick the project, produce it, equip the station -- one page.
- `app/src/pages/Documents.tsx` — Documents: the texts written for a project.
- `app/src/pages/Library.tsx` — Library: everything the project produced, in 2D and in 3D.
- `app/src/pages/Lookdev.tsx` — The universe: the game's art direction, shown element by element, dressed as the game.
- `app/src/pages/Showcase.tsx` — The showcase: the game's icons or props, shown as they are, to be critiqued.
- `app/src/pages/Vfx.tsx` — VFX: effect concepts, and their handoff to an agent who builds them in Godot.
- `app/src/pages/Viewport.tsx` — 3D viewport: the 3D step of a world card, not a page without context.
- `app/src/pages/Workbench.tsx` — A world card's workbench: the card, its concepts, its 3D.
- `app/src/pages/World.tsx` — World: the sections the user declares, and their cards.
- `app/src/update.tsx` — The update window: what the studio shows at startup when its code has changed.

## Tauri shell — `app/src-tauri/src/`

- `app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` — Application shell: two windows, and the studio server behind them.
- `app/src-tauri/src/main.rs` — The binary's entry point: it runs the shell defined in `lib.rs`.
- `app/src-tauri/src/server.rs` — Lifecycle of the Python server.
- `app/src-tauri/src/update.rs` — The update: the application follows the studio's code, at startup and while running.

## Scripts — `scripts/`

- `scripts/smoke_3d.py` — End-to-end test of the 3D pipeline, without calling Runware or an agent.
